title: The Alert Desk
tagline: Repeated alarms become one case. Only the critical ones interrupt me.
what: A Discord bot and an inbox page I built for the alarms my home servers raise. The bot merges repeats before they post, the inbox files each problem as a case with its own history, and only a short list of real trouble is allowed to page me.
built: Wrote a Discord bot that sorts every alert into the right channel and merges the repeats
Built the inbox page, where each alert and automated email becomes a case with its own history
Made email the last resort: only a critical failure, the first time it happens, emails me
Loaded in 30 days of old Discord alerts and 19 emails, with 62 automated tests behind it
credit: I wrote the bot and the inbox; Discord carries the messages

making.problem: Repeated server alarms buried the things I needed to act on. I wanted one place to read each problem and its history.
how: A small bot gets every alert first. It waits a bit before posting, merges repeats, and silences anything that keeps switching on and off.
A desk page files each alert as a case with a history, so the same problem is one case, not fifty messages.
Rules decide what is allowed to page me: only down services, a damaged storage pool, a full disk or a failed backup.
An AI helper can read a case and write up the likely cause.
credits: Everything else: me, with Claude as my pair programmer

log.text: Built and deployed the alert bot.
Put the alert senders through one route, so repeats merge before posting.
Started the inbox for alerts and automated emails.
Imported the older alerts and set a short list of failures allowed to email me.

serviceRecord.purpose: One problem, one case. Server alarms and automated mail arrive at a desk that keeps their history and decides what needs me.

receipt.title: It watched the watchers.
receipt.text: The desk filed four missing daily reports on its own during a slow-network morning. I could see the missed runs in the same place as the server alarms, without checking each report separately.

serviceRecord.care: Keep the interruption bar high. Down services, damaged storage, a full disk or a failed backup can page me.

entries.text: Built and deployed the alert bot. Server alarms now had a place to go.
Put the alert senders through one route, so repeats merge before they reach Discord.
Brought 19 emails and 30 days of Discord history into the desk. Each problem keeps its own case history.

back.pitch: A quieter inbox for a busy home lab. Repeated alarms become one case, and only a short list of critical first-time failures can send me an email.
cut: Discord carries the messages; my bot sorts them before they post.
An inbox that keeps each problem’s history together.
